gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Nextcloud All-in-One calls the Docker Engine API at a pinned v1.44 by default, while Synology's Container Manager is still built on Docker Engine 24.0.2 (newest build 24.0.2-1707, 2026-11-05), whose highest API is 1.43. On the DS925+ and DS225+, AIO therefore needs an SSH install with a DOCKER_API_VERSION override that Nextcloud says it does not support. UGREEN's UGOS Pro ships Engine 29.6.2, which needs no override.
standout_why: Pages compared: racksandwatts.com best-nas-for-a-homelab-2026 (cited) and nasdrives.ca best-nas-for-nextcloud-canada. Neither mentions Docker Engine or API versions, DOCKER_API_VERSION or Nextcloud AIO. Racksandwatts only says 'DSM Container Manager' and 'UGOS Pro Docker'. The cited nextcloud/all-in-one readme has part of it: its Synology section says 'you likely need to adjust the internally used api version' and that the Synology Docker GUI won't work for this. It gives no version numbers, and nothing in it ties the problem to Synology's frozen 24.0.2 engine or shows that UGREEN and QNAP aren't affected. In the 2026-11-08 chat ChatGPT reduced this to 'requires some manual configuration'. Our current page says 'AIO in Container Manager' for Synology, which suggests the GUI route works.
decides: It confirms UGREEN (DXP2800 / DXP4800 Plus) as the pick for Nextcloud AIO and pushes the Synology DS925+ down. DS925+ owners can't use AIO's default, supported setup from the Container Manager GUI. They need SSH or Task Scheduler as root, a custom socket path and DOCKER_API_VERSION=1.43, which the AIO readme says is not supported or tested by the maintainers. One DSM owner on Container Manager 24.0.2 reported the AIO mastercontainer warning that 'only v1.44 is officially supported' and AppAPI failing in a loop. QNAP (Engine 27.1.2) and TerraMaster (27.2.1) are above API 1.44, so the default works there. Shoppers who stay on Synology should be told to plan for the override, or to use the community nextcloud/docker image with Compose, which doesn't drive the Docker API.

findings.label: Docker Engine API version pinned by the Nextcloud AIO mastercontainer
findings.note: Source line: `private const string API_VERSION = 'v1.44';`. Requests go to http://127.0.0.1/<apiVersion>/<url>, so the version is fixed in the path and not negotiated. An env var DOCKER_API_VERSION overrides it.

findings.label: AIO's own position on overriding the API version
findings.value: Override with --env DOCKER_API_VERSION=…; 'only the default api version (unset this variable) is supported'
findings.note: FAQ section 'How to adjust the internally used docker api version?'. It also says: 'If you run an outdated or too new docker version, you might run into problems'.

findings.label: AIO's Synology DSM instructions
findings.value: Socket at /volume1/docker/docker.sock plus WATCHTOWER_DOCKER_SOCKET_PATH; 'you likely need to adjust the internally used api version'; Synology Docker GUI 'will not work', so run via SSH or a root Task Scheduler script
findings.source_title: all-in-one/readme.md at main · nextcloud/all-in-one (section 'How to run AIO on Synology DSM')
findings.note: Read through the raw readme. This is the part the cited readme already gives a reader. The engine numbers below are what it leaves out.

findings.label: Container Manager versions (engine version is the package-name prefix)
findings.source_title: Synology Release Notes for Container Manager (DSM 7 series)
findings.note: Synology's own release-notes feed. The release notes don't name the engine version in their text. Every build carries the 24.0.2 prefix, and Marius Hosting states 'Docker Engine version: 24.0.2' for Synology (next finding).

findings.label: Highest Docker Engine API version by engine release
findings.value: Engine 24.0: max API 1.43; Engine 25.0: max 1.44; Engine 29.3–29.8: max 1.54–1.55, min 1.40
findings.source_title: Docker Docs: Engine API version matrix
findings.note: So Synology's Engine 24.0.2 can't serve the v1.44 requests AIO sends by default. Every engine from 25.0 up can.

findings.label: Owner-reported AIO failure on DSM
findings.value: Mastercontainer: 'DOCKER_API_VERSION was found to be set to 1.43 … only v1.44 is officially supported'; AppAPI daemon 'docker_aio' not accessible, 300+ errors per minute
findings.source_title: AppAPI connection failure on Synology DSM (Docker API 1.43 vs 1.44 requirement) · Issue #7365 · nextcloud/all-in-one
findings.note: Opened 2026-01-01, closed by maintainer szaimen 2026-01-05 with a pointer to the nextcloud/app_api repo, locked 2026-01-20. The reporter worked around it by unchecking 'Docker Socket Proxy' in AIO; that isn't an official fix. The DS224+ is a different model running the same Container Manager package as the DS925+ and DS225+.
